source: Wikimedia Commons File:Japanese_Street_Signs_(27593276243).jpg, CC0 (photographer franck injapan, Tokyo), photographed 2016-07-09. Frozen 2026-07-11.
sentinel_for: domain-diverse entry: DENSE small-print Japanese text on an administrative/public-notice sign — deliberately the HARD case (no English backup text, obscure regional content), testing honest recall rather than assuming perfect translation.
notes: A Saitama Prefecture rabies-prevention association public notice (埼玉県狂犬病予防協会) on pet ownership rules: three numbered panels with cartoon illustrations (a crying dog+cat being abandoned in a box, a collar/leash circle, a waste pile) each captioned in Japanese, plus a bottom line about registration/vaccination. DELIBERATELY MODEST expectations — this is dense small-print administrative Japanese with no romanized backup text, unlike the Chinese entry; ground truth here only asserts what's visually verifiable without fluent Japanese (the illustration content), not precise translation of the prose. UNCALIBRATED by design. Companion to the Chinese entry: together they test both the 'romanized backup available' and 'no backup, honest recall only' cases. CALIBRATED 2026-07-11 after first scored run: the '<language> text' must_not entries were removed — they correctly caught natural descriptive prose ('written in Chinese characters', alongside a CORRECT full transcription), which is good behavior, not the lazy-tag pattern they were meant to guard against. The REAL lazy-tag pattern (bare tags like 'korean text banners' with no actual transcription) showed up on the Korean/Russian entries specifically and is now fixed at the source in tag_filter.clean_tag (language+generic-textual-word tags dropped, same pattern as the existing watermark/overlay junk filter) rather than tracked per-entry.
